name: Michele Stroh

positions.statement: On her campaign website, Stroh says groceries, gas, housing and childcare all cost more, and that Salem's answer is always another tax.
positions.excerpt: Groceries, gas, housing, childcare — everything costs more, and Salem’s answer is always another tax.

verification.note: Present in the opening 'A call for common-sense governance' section; curly apostrophe in 'Salem’s' matches the excerpt.

positions.statement: On the campaign website, the opening section begins with the line 'Oregonians are working harder and getting less.'
positions.excerpt: Oregonians are working harder and getting less.

verification.note: Loose general line: the opening sentence of the 'A call for common-sense governance' section, stating no policy or position. Statement reworded to say it is a general line in that section and to claim nothing about economic policy.

positions.statement: On the campaign website, the Real Results on Homelessness section begins: 'Oregon has spent billions and the crisis has grown.'
positions.excerpt: Oregon has spent billions and the crisis has grown.

verification.note: Excerpt is the first line of the 'Real Results on Homelessness' section; 'crisis' is homelessness only by the section context. Statement now names the section and quotes the line.

positions.statement: On the campaign website, the Real Results on Homelessness section includes treatment for addiction among its approaches, under the line 'Compassion means results.'
positions.excerpt: Compassion means results — treatment for addiction

verification.note: Excerpt is a fragment inside the 'Real Results on Homelessness' section, which lists several approaches; it is not confirmed as a heading. Statement reworded to say the section includes treatment for addiction among its approaches and no more.

positions.statement: On the campaign website, Stroh says that when she couldn't find the right childcare, she left the banking world to start a small business.
positions.excerpt: When I couldn’t find the right childcare, I left the banking world to start a small business

verification.note: Statement used 'they' for a first-person line from the candidate's biography section ('Hey, I'm Michele Stroh'). Reworded to 'she' and quoted.

positions.statement: On the campaign website, Stroh says they left banking to start a small business after not finding the right childcare.
positions.excerpt: I left the banking world to start a small business

verification.note: Duplicate of michele-stroh-i5: the excerpt is the second half of the same sentence and adds no small-business policy or position beyond her personal story already captured under childcare.

gaps: local-business: no standalone small-business policy found; the only mention is her childcare/small-business story (2026-10-19)
